nodes.name: Operating System Fundamentals

topics.title: Memory management: paging and virtual memory

miniTasks: Write a program that creates processes and threads and observe their behaviour.
Simulate FCFS, SJF and Round Robin and compare average waiting times.
Simulate a page-replacement algorithm (FIFO, LRU) and count faults.

resources.provider: Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau & Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau
resources.why: Free textbook covering virtualization, concurrency, persistence, and OS mechanisms.

resources.title: GeeksforGeeks Operating Systems
resources.why: Broad topic-wise OS notes useful for revision of processes, threads, scheduling, synchronization, memory, and filesystems.

resources.title: Gate Smashers – Operating System Complete Playlist
resources.why: Exact Gate Smashers OS playlist covering introduction, processes, threads, scheduling, synchronization, memory management, disk scheduling and file systems.

resources.title: Neso Academy – Operating System Playlist
resources.why: Specific Neso Academy OS playlist with a structured sequence from fundamentals through process management and memory.

resources.title: Gate Smashers – System Calls in Operating System
resources.why: Specific lesson explaining system calls and the transition from user mode to kernel functionality.

resources.title: Neso Academy – Introduction to Operating Systems
resources.why: Specific Neso Academy lecture covering the definition, types, functions and goals of an operating system.

resources.title: xv6 Operating System
resources.why: Small educational Unix-like kernel useful for understanding processes, memory, system calls, and filesystems.

resources.title: Linux man-pages
resources.why: Primary reference for system calls, processes, files, networking, and Linux interfaces.

resources.title: NPTEL – Operating System Fundamentals
resources.why: IIT lecture catalog useful for process management, memory, synchronization, and OS internals.

resources.title: CS 162: Operating Systems and System Programming
resources.why: CS 162: Operating Systems and System Programming directly supports operating systems preparation for top-tier technology and product interviews.

resources.title: Modern Operating Systems
resources.why: Modern Operating Systems directly supports operating systems preparation for top-tier technology and product interviews.

resources.title: The Linux Programming Interface
resources.why: The Linux Programming Interface directly supports operating systems / linux preparation for top-tier technology and product interviews.

nodes.name: Concurrency, Deadlocks and File Systems
miniTasks: Solve the producer-consumer problem with semaphores.
Write a small tool that walks a directory tree and reports file sizes.

resources.title: CS110: Principles of Computer Systems
resources.why: Covers processes, concurrency, threads, synchronization, networking, system calls, and Unix-oriented systems programming.

resources.title: Nand2Tetris Project 12 – Operating System
resources.why: Implement core Jack OS libraries to see how language abstractions map onto lower-level hardware and runtime services.

resources.title: OSDev Wiki – Bare Bones
resources.why: Guides the first bootable x86 kernel skeleton, exposing bootloading, cross-compilers, linking, and low-level systems concepts.

resources.title: Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System
resources.why: Introduces the happened-before relation and logical-clock ordering used to reason about events in distributed systems.

resources.title: The UNIX Time-Sharing System
resources.why: Historical systems paper describing the design principles of UNIX and its time-sharing environment, valuable for OS foundations.
